plan: [ In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding risks winning at a negative payoff if the second-highest bid exceeds your value; underbidding risks losing when you would have earned positive surplus. With values redrawn independently each round and no learning value from signaling, the optimal long-run profit strategy is truthful bidding each round. Therefore, set bid equal to my value, 26, which is my maximum willingness to pay. ]

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction, the weakly dominant strategy is truthful bidding. Bidding my value ensures I win precisely when the second-highest competing bid is below my value, and I pay that second-highest price, maximizing expected profit. No history to exploit; one round only. My value is 18, so I bid 18 to capture all profitable wins. ]

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding risks winning at a price above your value if the second-highest bid falls between your value and your inflated bid, yielding negative profit. Underbidding risks losing profitable auctions where the price would have been below your value. There’s only 1 round and no history to learn from. With value $21, bid exactly 21 to maximize expected profit. ]
